Whale distortion introduces a behavioral layer, modeling how large actors skew belief states. Informativeness scoring filters these signals, identifying moves that carry genuine predictive value. Together, they define a dual regime: one where capital flows are optimized via growth expectations, and another where belief integrity is preserved through signal validation. Failure modes include overfitting to estimation error, misidentification of manipulation, and loss of calibration when ω1 thresholds are violated. The system must balance exploration (stake) with exploitation (filter) while maintaining robustness to adversarial inputs.
